note: Committee composition is limited to 21 people, the majority of whom will be Brooklyn Community Board 6 Board Members, with others being Non-Board, or Public, Members of the committee. Term of appointment is for one (1) year effective September 1st.

committees.name: Landmarks, Land Use & Housing
committees.meets: Fourth Thursday of the month, 6:30 PM
committees.description: Oversees local land use, zoning, and development actions that undergo public review through the City's Uniform Land Use Review Procedure (ULURP), as well as Special Permit and Variance applications. Engages with private and public housing policy, development, stabilization, and mandatory inclusionary housing. Also assesses Landmarks Preservation Commission alteration applications within the district's three historic districts: Carroll Gardens, Cobble Hill, and Park Slope.

committees.name: Transportation, Parks, Public Infrastructure, and Public Safety
committees.meets: Third Wednesday of the month, 6:30 PM
committees.description: Reviews projects, studies, programs, policy initiatives, and services that affect neighborhood circulation, pedestrian and cyclist infrastructure, street greening, safe road sharing, open spaces and pedestrian plazas, mass transit accessibility, and recreational and cultural offerings in the public realm. Addresses intermodal transportation issues including public transit, truck routes, highways and tunnels. Public parks and the nonprofits that help manage them, privately owned public spaces, community gardens, and street greening fall under the committee. Oversees emergency services delivery, including the 76th and 78th Precincts, Housing PSA 1, Transit Districts 30 and 32, Fire, and EMS.

committees.name: Business Affairs and Licenses
committees.meets: Fourth Monday of the month, 6:30 PM
committees.description: Works to enhance the district's local economy and balance it with the quality of life of commercial neighbors. Regularly reviews State Liquor Authority license applications for bars, restaurants, and venues offering onsite liquor consumption. Provides a space for City agencies and organizations to share information that strengthens services to small business owners, and a forum for merchants, merchant associations, and Business Improvement Districts.

committees.name: Human Services and Environmental Sustainability
committees.meets: Third Tuesday of the month, 6:30 PM
committees.description: Addresses community needs and environmental concerns within the district. Dedicated to youth, library, educational, and public health programs and services, and reviews and recommends funding for youth and community development initiatives. Focuses on social and healthcare services for the district's general, youth, senior, NYCHA, and special needs populations. Also addresses environmental quality: urban heat island effects, air quality, stormwater management, solid waste and water quality management, and alternative energy systems.

committees.name: Budget Subcommittee
committees.description: Overseen by the Executive Committee's Treasurer and made up solely of Board Members. Coordinates the annual Statement of District Needs, which the board submits to the City each fall as part of the budget process for the upcoming fiscal year.

committees.name: BMT Subcommittee
committees.description: Executive subcommittee on the Brooklyn Marine Terminal redevelopment.

key_note: Codes after a name are that member's committees. * marks a chair or co-chair.
